title: Connect Wire Envelope
description: The outer envelope wrapping every message exchanged between a Mac and an Android device over the Connect wire protocol. Every message, regardless of feature, is serialized as JSON matching this shape after Noise decryption (see docs/wire-protocol.md). The `type` field selects a registered message type (see schema/message-types.md); `payload` is validated ad hoc per type, not by this schema.

v.description: Envelope schema version. Bump only on a breaking change to this envelope shape (not on new message types, which are additive).

id.description: Unique identifier for this message instance, used for de-duplication, correlation, and ack/response matching.

type.description: Dotted namespace string identifying the message's purpose, e.g. 'handshake.hello' or 'presence.heartbeat'. Must be a type registered in schema/message-types.md before it ships.

senderId.description: Stable device UUID of the device that produced this message. Every device has a stable UUID identity established at pairing time (see docs/architecture.md).

recipientId.description: Stable device UUID of the intended recipient, or null when the message is addressed by the `broadcast` flag instead of a specific device. In v1 there are only ever two trusted devices, but this field exists from day one so multi-device addressing (see docs/adr/0002-device-group-addressing.md) does not require a protocol rewrite later.

broadcast.description: When true, this message is addressed to all trusted devices in the local device group rather than a single recipientId. Flood-forwarded to every directly-connected peer (except whichever one it just arrived from) by every device that receives it, so it reaches devices with no direct connection to the sender — see the 'ttl' field and docs/wire-protocol.md's 'Multi-hop relay' section.

ttl.description: Hop budget for flood-forwarding across the mesh. Set to 8 (the default) by the originating sender, decremented by 1 at every relaying hop (a device forwarding an envelope it did not itself originate), and dropped (not forwarded further, though still delivered locally if addressed to that hop) once it reaches 0. See docs/wire-protocol.md's 'Multi-hop relay' section for the full algorithm.

ts.description: Sender-local timestamp the message was created, in Unix epoch milliseconds.

payload.description: Type-specific message body. Its shape is defined per `type` in schema/message-types.md and is intentionally not validated by this schema.
